title: At a convenience store
summary: Find things, make polite requests, accept or decline service, and say how you will pay.
sourceFiles: コンビニの会話　初級　at a convenience store.pdf
takeaways: ください asks for a thing or action; お願いします makes a flexible polite request.
で marks the payment method just like another means.
は can contrast what you need with what you do not.

grammar.title: Ask for a thing or action
grammar.pattern: Noun をください / Verb てください
grammar.summary: Use noun + をください for an item. Use a て-form + ください to request an action.

grammar.title: Contrast what you need
grammar.summary: Use は to put two items in contrast. が can join two clauses with a soft “but.”

examples.english: I do not need a bag, but I do need chopsticks.

grammar.caution: This clause-joining が is different from the subject-marker が. Context reveals the job.

grammar.title: Pay by a method
grammar.summary: The means particle で covers cards, cash, transit cards, tools, vehicles, and languages.

recall.prompt: How do you request a noun politely?
recall.answer: Noun をください or Noun をお願いします

recall.prompt: Which particle marks how you pay?
What does そのままで大丈夫です mean in context?
recall.answer: It is fine as it is; no change or extra service is needed.
